notes: The same virtual monitor reaches commit-modes and assign-swapchain when the experimental render adapter is removed and no render preference is requested. Desktop surfaces are received at 1024x768 BGRA8. This isolates monitor viability; it does not establish that every failure with the experimental renderer has the same cause.

The first host reaches the IddCx watchdog breakpoint. A simultaneous thread stack shows Direct3D device construction inside the driver assign-swapchain callback. The breakpoint pauses the VM and interrupts WinRM; the debugger resumes without changing watchdog settings. The framework reports fatal driver error 0x50100040000010f and starts another host.
The completed consumer records report 14 and 28 received frames; an interrupted consumer has no final count, so these are not an exact run total. No image is displayed by this diagnostic sink.
The installed device remains observable as started after host recovery; that status alone is not evidence of uninterrupted operation. The exact owned device and package are removed afterward.
A subsequent source revision prepares and retains the Direct3D device before monitor arrival, using a framework work item. Its live behavior is tested separately.
